title: AI Risk Management Framework FAQs | NIST

policy_extraction.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
covered_actors: organizations of all sizes, public or private, in any sector

evidence.quote: intended to help developers, users and evaluators of AI systems better manage AI risks which could affect individuals, organizations, society, or the environment
foster the development of innovative approaches to address characteristics of trustworthiness including ... accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable
Framework users and AI actors should consider and encompass trustworthiness characteristics during pre-design, design and development, deployment, use, and test and evaluation
NIST has produced the AI RMF as a voluntary Framework
evidence.source_section: Will private or public sector organizations be required to use the Framework?

evidence.quote: Organizations seeking specific guidance for how to achieve AI RMF function outcomes may borrow as many – or as few – suggestions as apply to their industry use case or interests

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: The AI RMF is explicitly voluntary; Congress directed NIST to develop it as such. A companion Playbook provides actionable suggestions. No penalties or enforcement mechanisms are specified.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document primarily frames AI governance as a matter of managing risks to individuals, organizations, society, and the environment through trustworthiness characteristics (safe, reliable, fair, privacy-enhanced, etc.). This aligns most closely with consumer/public safety framing. Secondary frames include innovation enablement (supporting trustworthy AI development) and economic competitiveness (enhancing economic security).

evidence_spans.quote: intended to help developers, users and evaluators of AI systems better manage AI risks which could affect individuals, organizations, society, or the environment
evidence_spans.source_section: What is the AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF)?

evidence_spans.quote: aims to cultivate trust in the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI technologies and systems in ways that enhance economic security and improve quality of life
evidence_spans.source_section: Why has NIST developed the Framework?

evidence_spans.quote: foster the development of innovative approaches to address characteristics of trustworthiness including valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed
